counsel. - (pt) mr president, ladies and gentlemen, let me first of all emphasize that relations with the mediterranean countries are a priority established as such in the portuguese presidency's work programme for this six-month period. we are aware of the main mechanisms established by the european union in this area, which is why i will not mention them here. but i would like to say that during the portuguese presidency an informal meeting of foreign ministers on the subject of the euro-mediterranean partnership will take place on 25 and 26 may with a view to establishing a frank and open dialogue on the functioning and priorities of the partnership, more concretely by taking stock of and making a critical analysis of the way we read the terms of the functioning of the partnership - which, as we know, can give rise to different interpretations in certain states on either side of the mediterranean - so as to be able to give the necessary impetus to boost activities on all three fronts. the meeting will also aim to prepare the formal barcelona iv meeting of foreign ministers, which will take place in marseille in november as part of the barcelona process. we believe that this evaluation will be important not only to do systematically what we did in stuttgart but also to analyse the new priorities in certain areas where cooperation is not very developed. as regards the creation of a free trade area, which is one of the other aspects of the mediterranean policy process, we believe that it should not be seen as an end in itself, but rather as a means of improving the living conditions of citizens and increasing their level of performance. more specifically, it must help to reduce the disparities that exist today between the citizens of the european union. the creation of this area will undoubtedly provide the mediterranean countries, through a process of free trade, with the opportunity to become part of a more interdependent world and, consequently, not to remain on the sidelines of this global development towards greater prosperity and greater well-being. as regards the meda programme, which is an important instrument in this context, the amount of the meda-ii programme for the period 2000-06 is not yet known, and the commission has announced shortly short proposals for the allocation of the budget heading iv on external relations, which includes the meda programme. the council is analysing the proposal put forward by the commission at the end of last year to simplify and improve the procedures of the meda regulation, responding to a request from our mediterranean partners. we have observed in the past that, whether from certain partners in the southern mediterranean, from certain community countries, or from the commission itself - which has carried out a concrete assessment of the effectiveness of the system in this area - that this system needed to be improved in part. we believe that the mechanisms proposed can go in that direction. the european parliament has also been consulted on this proposal and the council is awaiting its opinion. the meda programme also finances activities in the fields of education and vocational training and, under the current framework, amounts to almost €1 billion per year. the european investment bank's borrowings, which represent an amount of the same order of magnitude, are mainly intended for the financing of infrastructure and environmental projects. i would add that on 31 march and 1 april a meeting of experts on employment and vocational training will take place as part of the barcelona process to study how to help the southern mediterranean countries to define national policies on employment and vocational training and to exchange information and experience. the main objective is obviously to contribute to an increase in competitiveness, since the latter depends largely on the level of vocational training. as regards the role of the high representative for the common foreign and security policy, which is the subject of one of the questions put to the council, i would like to say that the european union has attached great importance to promoting a coherent and comprehensive policy for the mediterranean region. in this area, we intend to play an active role not only in the context of the barcelona process but also in the middle east peace process. the high representative is particularly committed to this type of issue and participated in the last ministerial steering committee meeting in moscow, which gave a new impetus to the multilateral side of the middle east peace process, in which the european union is involved. as you know, the european union intends to continue to work on other issues, such as the development of a common strategy for the mediterranean policy, in accordance with what was decided at the cologne european council and reiterated at the helsinki european council. the portuguese presidency is currently preparing this joint strategy, which, and i would like to draw your attention to this, has different characteristics from the two previous joint strategies of a bilateral nature, either with russia or with ukraine. this is a common strategy of a more horizontal nature, with a multilateral character, and involving a number of actors who, in our view, must try to go beyond the content of the barcelona process. if the common strategy is just a repetition of what is found in the barcelona process, we will not add any value to a coherent policy on the part of the european union towards our partners in the south. our aim is to contribute, through the implementation of this common strategy, to giving it a new dimension and, more particularly, to taking account of the development of the middle east peace process and how this development - in a positive sense, we hope - can be reflected on the strategy itself within the mediterranean region. the european union is also working on a forward-looking document on the future of the region so as to be prepared to play its full role when peace is launched in the middle east peace process. an analysis of the issues where the european union is particularly well positioned in relation to security, water and refugee issues will also need to be implemented. as regards the euro-mediterranean charter for peace and stability, a subject which has been the subject of attention in this parliament and which is also the subject of attention in the council, work in this area was planned in the context of the mandate given by the stuttgart ministerial conference in april 1999 and meetings on this subject were held in november, december and march. the debate so far has focused on the principles to be included in the charter, the means and mechanisms for its implementation, and the institutional provisions. another meeting is due to take place in brussels in a few days' time on this subject. work is also progressing towards the preparation of a progress report, which will be analysed, albeit informally, at the meeting of foreign ministers to be held in lisbon during the portuguese presidency. the council does not, at this stage, and in answer to another question, consider the possibility of a multilateral treaty between third countries. the european union considers that any spontaneous form of south-south cooperation, the level of which is still very low, should be encouraged, as should the acceleration of trade agreements between the mediterranean countries, for which technical support has already been provided. and let me add, mr president, that in this area, a large part of the complaints about the way the mediterranean process is working almost always relate to the way north-south relations are being conducted. i would like to emphasize here, without criticism, that there is also a clear dimension that was defined in barcelona: there is a whole regional work to be done between the countries of the southern fringe of the mediterranean as regards their intra- and interregional relations, which has not been done, and which is also recognized by the countries of the southern mediterranean, and the euro-mediterranean cooperation process cannot succeed without this work of intra-regional cooperation in the southern mediterranean. and it is important that this message is also perceived by our partners in the south, because if it is not, we will never go beyond a kind of individualized vectors of the european union's relationship with each of these countries and we will never succeed in creating a common space; the eu's external relations are also very important for the mediterranean region, and this will only be achieved if the countries of the southern mediterranean understand that they must make concessions and maintain a constructive dialogue aimed at developing into intra-regional cooperation. i would also like to point out that the french presidency intends to continue the work already begun in the hague in march 1999 on migration and population exchange in the field of the euro-mediterranean partnership and will organise a meeting at senior civil servant level in the second half of this year. this is a highly sensitive issue and we recognise the importance and relevance of the question which has been put to the council, but the resolution of which requires good preparation. as regards the question of the target date of 2010 and the possibility of setting up a committee to study the necessary actions, we do not intend to set up such a committee at this time, but we are determined to continue and conclude as soon as possible the negotiations on the association agreements between the european union and the mediterranean countries. the conclusion of these agreements depends on the will of both parties. the association agreement with morocco has just entered into force on 1 march, and in view of the progress in national ratification, the presidency believes that the agreement with israel will also be able to enter into force next june. as is known, negotiations with algeria will continue in mid-april and they should have continued with syria at the end of march, but they have just been postponed due to the formation of the new government. the portuguese presidency hopes that significant progress can be made during this six-month period. on the other hand, mr president, it is also important to point out that we must adopt, in the context of these euro-mediterranean agreements, a perspective of systematic non-growth of the expectations envisaged in these same agreements. the euro-mediterranean agreements cannot be a kind of launching pad allowing the countries that conclude them to continue to enjoy substantial and cumulative advantages compared to what they have previously obtained, because this would give rise to a kind of systematic mirroring in this process. the countries of the southern mediterranean must understand that we must guarantee equal treatment and that we cannot take advantage of successive agreements by delaying the launch of the processes. the commission has not yet adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. it is not a process of accumulation, but rather a process of balance and fairness. the european union has tried to demonstrate to the countries of the southern mediterranean that the creation of the single market has been a positive experience. and that is why, in the context of what i have just said, we have urged these countries to try to harmonize their legislation as closely as possible with that of the union. this objective is part of the national industrial cooperation programme implemented in the framework of the euro-mediterranean partnership, and the portuguese presidency has decided, in collaboration with the government of cyprus, to hold a situation review at the level of the ministers of industry in nicosia on 21 and 23 june, which seems to us to be of the utmost importance. this will be the third euro-mediterranean meeting at the level of industry ministers in this field. the question put to the european parliament on the middle east peace process raises a fundamental problem. the visibility of the middle east peace process was not an end in itself for the european union. we consider that the key criterion underlying the action of the council of ministers is the attempt to contribute, through our presence and our action, to the success of the peace process. we have strongly supported this peace process, not only through substantial economic aid - and i would like to make it clear that this economic aid is not in parallel with what has been done in the middle east - but also through political initiatives and constructive support for the efforts led by the united states and other key players. but one thing must be borne in mind: the visibility and presence of the european union in the middle east peace process will be what the partners in the peace process want it to be, and not necessarily what might correspond to the visibility interest that some countries might have in this area. we will do everything in our power to be useful to this peace process, because it is peace that we are interested in and not necessarily visibility in the context of peace. i would like to emphasize our commitment to the palestinian side, which is expressed in support for the implementation of the agreements reached and in our contribution to the permanent status negotiations. as regards syria, the council is firmly continuing its work, particularly through a special envoy - whose extremely positive work i would like to emphasize - to help the two sides set out on the road to resuming bilateral negotiations, which, as you know, took place last december. we hope that the new international situation in syria can also bring about a positive change in the situation, given the interdependence of all the vectors in the middle east. the council worked together with the united states and russia, which together sponsored the multilateral aspect of the process which began in madrid in 1991, so that after a three-year break these activities could resume normally at this level. this effort led to a ministerial meeting of the steering group on 1 february, at which the green light was given to a majority of multilateral groups to resume normal activities this spring. the council and the commission will convene this group on 8 and 11 may as chairs of the working group on economic and regional development, which has 53 members from inside and outside the region. the european union will also host the next meeting of the steering group in july. with regard to the meeting of 24 january, the council invited the high representative to examine in greater depth, with the assistance of his special envoy and the commission, the issues on region, so that the european union is fully prepared to play an important role when peace is concluded. cooperation with civil society, which is one of the points raised in another question, remains at the lisbon meeting we will be able to look at where the activities of this third phase can be concentrated in order to allow civil society to play an increasingly important role in this area. the question of financial support for non-governmental organisations active in this field is of course a matter for the commission. as regards the arab maghreb union, the council was convinced of the have already said, regional cooperation in the maghreb through the political dialogue it maintains with algeria, tunisia and morocco. and since, apart from certain cyclical developments - which we hope will be temporarily limited - they may have had a negative influence on the relationship within the arab maghreb, we hope to see the situation develop positively in the future. as regards relations with libya, a major step forward was taken with the lifting of sanctions, with the exception of the arms embargo, last september. the council confirmed its wish to see libya fully involved in the barcelona process and hoped that it would be able to give full and unreserved agreement to the barcelona process. the troika at ambassador level has also just applied to libya on 26 and 27 march, and in this context it has been made clear to libya that if it accepts the barcelona process, it should negotiate an association agreement with the european union in order to be able to join the euro-mediterranean free trade area planned for 2010. the question of negotiating such an agreement with libya is not on the agenda at the moment, but the council will discuss it in due course. the council is aware of the challenges posed by private investment, which is one of the key levers for growth. following the portuguese proposal put forward in the mediterranean forum and then continued in the barcelona process, a conference on investment across the mediterranean area was held from 28 february to 11 march, with a significant private sector participation. participants highlighted the low and insufficient level of investment flows in the mediterranean region compared to other regions of the world, given its potential. they also stressed the various investment-friendly factors which need to be brought together and strengthened, in particular the need to create a sufficient market dimension, which will be achieved by the creation of a progressive euro-mediterranean free trade area. on that occasion, the commission announced the creation of a euro-mediterranean network of cooperation between investment promotion agencies, which should enable it to be updated and institutionally strengthened through a training and know-how programme. a study on the obstacles to foreign direct investment has also been launched, which we believe should provide us with reliable data by the end of the year. on the question of western sahara, which is dealt with in another question, the council supported the efforts of the un secretary-general and his special representative for the region, ambassador eagleton, and his special envoy, mr bacon. the council has taken note of the report presented by mr bacon on 17 february that the timetable is no longer valid and that at this stage it has not yet been possible to set a new date for the referendum with certainty. we are well aware that this new circumstance can be a negative element in the whole process. the council can, however, only welcome the intention of the high representative to ask his special envoy to explore ways and means of achieving an acceptable and lasting solution to this conflict. the council confirms its readiness to contribute to the creation of a climate of confidence between all parties in order to find a solution to the question of western sahara based on human rights and respect for democratic principles. i shall now conclude, mr president. but i happen to be answering a very long series of questions and of course if i do not elaborate enough on the various questions, some members might think that the portuguese presidency does not attach any importance to them. i mean, we have presented in detail, although this topic deserves in my view to be developed more widely, some of the different elements of the current mediterranean policy. however, there may be a feeling of disappointment about the expectations that followed the launch of the barcelona process in november 1995 - and i am perhaps one of the only ones here who participated in the launch of the agreement - mainly because of the political circumstances in the middle east, which were favourable in november 1995 but have since deteriorated sharply with the blockade of the peace process. we must not forget, however, that despite these difficulties, the barcelona process can continue, and i think it is important to stress that it is the only body that brings together the arab mediterranean countries, israel and the european union around the same table, which in my view is already a remarkable progress in itself. we believe that with the new israeli government in office and its new policy of relaunching the peace process, we can once again hope that there will be positive repercussions on the development of the middle east peace process.
commission. - mr president, i would like to make the following remarks on behalf of my colleague, mr chris patten. the commission shares the view that the barcelona process needs to be given new impetus and will shortly be presenting new ideas which should enable us to take the process forward this year, particularly in the light of the euro-mediterranean summit which is likely to take place in mid-november. agreement on the text of the charter for peace and stability is expected to be reached at the meeting in mid-november. it should be as meaningful and as far-reaching as possible. i would also like to see regular discussions on security and stability open to all partners who wish to participate. we should also develop cooperation on drugs, terrorism, immigration, good governance and conflict prevention, at least with the maghreb countries. i also want this partnership to take on a greater human rights dimension. we should have a frank and open dialogue on the policies that partner governments should pursue to improve the situation in this area. we will use meda and the meda specific programme for democracy to support positive actions, in particular those carried out by ngos, to promote respect for human rights and democratic freedoms in the region. the economic objective of the partnership is to create a common area of prosperity through the progressive establishment of free trade, with substantial eu financial support for economic transition and to help the partners meet the social and economic challenges that this entails. meda-funded programmes are in place to support industrial modernisation, structural adjustment, private sector development, training and promotion of small and medium-sized enterprises. all programmes contain conditionality clauses ensuring that their social impacts are taken into account. i intend in future to give greater weight to the priorities in our financial cooperation, in particular by focusing on sectoral adjustment aid. these will allow us to focus on the key objectives of the partnership and will also improve the disbursement rate for meda. the implementation of meda has been the subject of criticism, some justified, some not. it is a young programme with specific objectives relating to the implementation of free trade with partners. often, partner governments are not the final beneficiaries, which in itself has increased the complexity of implementation. the commission has put forward a proposal to amend the meda regulation to ensure a more strategic approach to programming, better coordination with other donors, including member states, and streamlining procedures. the proposal is still under discussion in the council and i fear that, far from supporting these objectives, the council is moving towards a burdening of procedures. i am counting on parliament to support our efforts. i would also like to see the commission's internal procedures reformed in order to speed up the achievement of results. investment is a crucial issue which was addressed at the important conference held in lisbon on 29 february and 1 march. the conference showed that the key to increasing the region's attractiveness to investors is that the partners have thriving, open, competitive economies within a secure and predictable legal and administrative environment. we will use meda to support the partners' efforts in this regard. it is also vital that regional cooperation ensures that the region has a unified market. free trade areas at the subregional level should be supported as a step towards the overall objective. i want to encourage the harmonization of measures relating to a single market among all the partners - an agreement on an action programme is expected later this year - and to offer diagonal cumulation of rules of origin to partners who agree to practice free trade between them. regional infrastructure is essential for economic development. the meda programme supports, among other things, the interconnection of infrastructure in the fields of energy, transport and new technologies. investment in these areas is mainly supported by loans from the european investment bank and other donors. i will continue to ensure that the appropriate dosage of funding is used so that the public and private sectors can play their part. as far as agriculture is concerned, all the issues relating to this sector should be given full consideration, bearing in mind what we can do to improve market access and with free trade as the objective. in addition, we are considering the introduction of a regional cooperation programme which could focus on processing and conservation, quality standards and animal health. support for civil society is essential for the development of the human dimension of the partnership. i will make sure that civil society is supported, but as far as the old decentralised cooperation programmes are concerned, i will not repeat the mistakes of the past in terms of financial management and administration. ngos can benefit from a number of programmes, for example the smart programme on the environment, the cultural heritage programme, the euromed youth programme and the meda for democracy programme. i will consider what more we can do, while respecting the need for sound financial management.

- (es) mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it will be five years in november since the barcelona declaration was signed. the time has therefore come to take stock of the euro-mediterranean policy, to take stock of the results achieved, as well as of the delays and shortcomings. in this sense, this debate and the motions for resolutions tabled by the groups in this parliament are a very timely initiative. there are certainly positive aspects to this report. firstly - and this is not a small thing - the process has continued, despite the negative circumstances in which the middle east peace process has been placed. the summits and meetings have always been held, and in the presence of all the countries concerned, including syria, lebanon and israel. then there was also the signing, ratification and implementation of a series of association agreements, albeit slowly. finally, a routine of permanent intergovernmental cooperation was developed and projects for the various meda financial aids were implemented. but these results cannot ignore the delays and shortcomings which partly disappointed the hopes and prospects created by the first euro-mediterranean conference in november 1995. firstly, there was no decisive political impulse when it was absolutely necessary. in fact, it could now be said that mediterranean policy should be the first priority of the european union's foreign policy. eastern enlargement, in strategic and historical terms, leads to a scenario with no uncertainties other than those relating to timing, pace, costs and means; even if we admit the possibility of new regional conflicts, it is very difficult to imagine any other scenario than the culmination of the enlargement process. however, there is no certainty as to the future of the mediterranean basin. whether this region becomes a sun belt, with economic and social rebalancing in a context of security, development and peace, or a slum belt, where the norm is the growing imbalance between the north and the south, rampant poverty in the south and the gradual emergence - forgive me for being redundant - of all kinds of emergencies, such as violence, instability, terrorism and migratory pressures that cannot be contained, depends largely on the policy developed by the european union. secondly, i believe that as a result of this lack of political management, the economic and financial dimension has encountered obstacles and delays. in this connection, it is worth noting the difficulties in launching the meda programmes, the excessive centralisation, the heterogeneity of the aid criteria, the lack of common thinking on the possibility of a common mediterranean agricultural policy and, finally, as a consequence of all this, the low level of direct investment in the south, which represents only 2% of all direct investment of the european union abroad. and this illustrates what we might call the 'strategic blindness' of the european system as a whole. in conclusion, we need a new stage, with the portuguese and french presidencies, a brand new start for euro-mediterranean policy, which can bring a virtuous circle towards the objectives that the euro-mediterranean conference of barcelona in november 1995 correctly defined.

commissioner, the very implementation of these action plans is already a positive step. the combination of actions in the field of foreign policy, cooperation and development and the adoption of measures to organize migration flows is also positive. but i think the way in which the council has presented these plans to parliament has not been positive, because it has acted like a statue of human rights are being constantly violated, in addition to the political instability of these countries. the case of morocco, albania or sri lanka is special because these countries offer more opportunities for multi-sectoral cooperation, and there are even privileged situations, as in the case of morocco, where an association agreement has just been launched. in addition to the fact that development cooperation in the selected countries, including integration measures. we cannot criminalize immigration, whether it is political or economic. we therefore believe that it is urgent to implement the provisions of the amsterdam treaty and the tampere summit on the 'communitarisation' of asylum policy and the fair and humane treatment of refugees and immigrants. the human conditions sensitive to european society today as immigration and asylum depends on the success of these plans.

- (es) mr president, i am afraid that my opinion does not coincide with that of mr harbour or mr wuermeling, because, considering that the 1985 directive on civil liability is a landmark in consumer protection and an area where the commission's work has been very important and has had a progressive tendency, i believe that many years have already passed since its approval in 1985. i think it is therefore worth pointing out and applauding the fact that the commission has considered revising it. this green paper is a first step towards that revision. it must be borne in mind that in 1985 certain principles which are now considered essential were not introduced and could not have been incorporated into the text of the directive at that time because the debate was not sufficiently mature. the first of these principles is that it is necessary to point out the need for the manufacturer to assume, at least in some respects, the risk of development. i come from a country, spain, where consumer legislation obliges the manufacturer to take responsibility for the risk of development. neither the insurance company nor any manufacturer went bankrupt, and this did not prevent technical progress. the consumer must no longer be the only one to pay for this risk of progress, this must change. the second principle is to relieve the injured party of the burden of proof. we are talking about objective responsibility and we must therefore reduce the burden of proof on the victim as much as possible. the third principle is that of quantifying the damage. this possibility is provided for in the directive but it must be borne in mind that the courts generally call this quantification of damage interference by the legislature in its functions and this point must therefore also be revised.

proposed a multiannual community action plan to promote safer use of the internet by combating illegal and dangerous content on global networks. the council and parliament adopted it on 25 january 1999. the action plan supports concrete measures in four areas: a european telephone assistance network, industry self-regulation, filtering, and training and awareness-raising. in addition, the commission, i.e. the union, is involved in the work of the g8 to set up a network of 24-hour contact points. it is also involved in the negotiations within the council of europe on a draft convention on cybercrime which will deal with the specific problem of child pornography on the internet. the commission fully supports the position expressed in the draft report that child pornography on the internet requires the harmonization of the laws and regulations of the member states. we are convinced that agreements must be reached on common definitions, offences and sanctions for certain types of crime. we have included in the scoreboard of the area of freedom, security and justice a specific action to criminalise the sexual exploitation of children and in particular child pornography on the internet, as requested by the heads of state and government at the european summit in tampere. a proposal for a framework decision on common definitions, common offences and common sanctions will be presented after the summer. the commission will participate fully in the discussions in the council with a view to the adoption of this draft decision, in order to examine whether further action is necessary. we approve parliament's proposal on the legal basis: as a framework decision, it must be based on article 34 (2) (b) of the treaty. the commission will also consider, with the member states, ways of supporting the implementation of the decision through other projects funded under the stop programme. these could be aimed at further promoting training and exchanges between the authorities responsible for combating this phenomenon in the member states, such as the police, but also the judiciary, and close cooperation between these authorities, europol and the future eurojus network. finally, the commission would like to tell parliament that it can fully support all the amendments tabled by mr kirkhope and the committee on civil liberties and internal affairs, as they bring some very useful clarifications on the definitions and description of the activities to be criminalised, on the age limit, on the offence of detention and on the need for the police and judicial authorities to adopt the technological instruments necessary to secure the internet and to make the fight against child pornography not just a matter of rhetoric but a concrete action undertaken by - the next item is the report (a5-0091/2000) by mrs frahm, on behalf of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, on the proposal for a council decision establishing a european refugee fund (com (99) 686 - c5-0120/2000 - 1999/0274 (cns)).
- (es) mr president, first of all i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mrs frahm, because i think she has done a really good job. the report also reflects the satisfaction of parliament. the creation of this fund is good news for us. we have been trying to develop a coherent approach to this since 1997 and we are already achieving some successes. in any case, if we are to be fully successful, we need a legal basis which ensures continuity of work on improving reception, the integration of refugees into the european union or, if they wish, their return under good conditions. these are three different lines of work. the three lines must be guaranteed and i am in favour of creating a reserve to deal with the arrival of displaced persons without jeopardising the development of better infrastructure and better practices within the union. as regards the allocation of resources, solidarity must be ensured with countries which show a high level of commitment in this area, but it must also be borne in mind - as the report says - the need for countries with a less important tradition of hosting - like mine - to improve their infrastructure and services to bring themselves up to par with the others and to assume - as i think that should be the aim - a greater share of responsibility alongside the other countries of the european union. the role and efforts of the member states in this respect are important. but i would point out that the experience of managing other funds, in particular the structural funds, should also be used to involve not only the member states but also local and regional authorities and civil society organisations in this management. this would be an added value, as contact with ngos and local administrations could contribute to the fight against racism, to the involvement of society and to informing citizens in the host countries about the importance of the right of asylum and the reception of refugees. in addition, the use of existing practices for the management of these funds could encourage interaction between them. we must have consistent policies for both funds. finally, i join those who are calling for an increase in the financial allocation of the european refugee fund.
the commission is aware of the fact that the commission has not yet adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. you know better than i do that the proposal for a council decision on this fund was adopted by the commission on 14 december 1999. it supports an approach, my own personal approach, which i put forward during the hearing before the committee on civil liberties and human rights of the european parliament. the fund brings together in a single instrument support for member states' actions in the field of reception, integration and voluntary repatriation of refugees and displaced persons, which were previously the subject of joint actions and pilot projects on the basis of appropriations entered annually in the budget of the communities at the initiative of the european parliament. the fund is not intended to replace the efforts of the member states in the area of reception and integration of refugees, but it is a first step which highlights an essential political aspect of a european strategy: the asylum strategy must be based on a shared responsibility at european level. i believe that the adoption of this fund helps to demonstrate that in this area the european union as such can add value to the efforts of each member state. we are setting up a european refugee fund for an initial period of five years. the financial envelope for 2000 is eur 36 million, of which eur 10 million is for emergency aid. i fully understand the rapporteur's remarks that this amount is insufficient in the face of the scale of the needs and ambitions of the fund itself. the commission has already informed the parliamentary committee on budgets of its intention to propose, in the preliminary draft budget for 2001, measures to ensure the financial sustainability of the fund for the next five years. in other words, the commission will propose to increase the budget from eur 36 million in 2000 to eur 45 million in the following years, bringing the overall allocation for the five years to eur 216 million. i think this is a first step in the right direction. the european refugee fund is an instrument of solidarity between the member states whose objective - as has already been stressed by several speakers - is to contribute to the balance of the efforts referred to in article 63 (2) (b) of the treaty. to this end, the resources are to be distributed proportionally between the member states: on the one hand, in proportion to the number of asylum seekers they receive (two thirds of the resources) and, on the other hand, in proportion to the number of refugees they host on their territory (one third of the resources). i understand why it was proposed to consider the number of refugees in relation to the total population of each member state. i must say that the commission itself has tried to consider this criterion, but it has been extremely difficult for us to find a mathematical formula which can really respect the principle of burden and effort sharing by including this criterion. i am quite willing to consider concrete solutions, but we must not stop at the statement of principle. we must find a practical solution, and i must admit that it is not easy. the european refugee fund will be able to co-finance member states' actions up to a maximum of 50%, a proportion that may be increased to 75% in member states covered by the cohesion fund. the proposal also provides for the possibility of financing emergency measures in the event of a massive influx of refugees from the reserve of eur 10 million. in this respect, it offers a first response to the request made by the european council in tampere. i have already started a discussion with my colleague michaele schreyer on how to mobilise, in the event of an emergency, larger resources adapted to the scale of the needs. but in this area, more than the figures - because, unfortunately or fortunately, we cannot foresee the amounts needed to respond to emergency situations such as kosovo - what concerns me and what we are looking for is a financial mechanism, and also an administrative one, sufficiently developed to respond effectively to requests in an emergency situation. the selection and management of the fund's projects, in its structural line, is delegated to the member states in the context of co-financing applications. the detailed rules for implementation, monitoring, monitoring and evaluation are based on the provisions in force for the structural funds. as regards the amendments, the commission has taken note of all the proposed amendments and can accept, subject in some cases to amendments of form, the principles which underlie a number of them and which are intended to clarify in the preamble the objectives of the european refugee fund or to make certain provisions more precise. this includes the recall in the preamble of the importance of the work of ngos, certain useful details, such as the transparency of the project selection process, or the need to promote the continuity of projects over time. the principle of a minimum contribution from the fund allows each member state, regardless of the size of the refugee flows, to provide effective support. the commission cannot, however, agree with other sets of amendments, in particular those relating to budgetary techniques. the commission's proposals to increase the fund's budget to eur 216 million over five years will be accepted by the budgetary authority. the commission cannot support the amendments concerning the member states' strategy and the establishment of a partnership with the various actors concerned by asylum policy. this is the first experience of a decentralised asylum programme. the national administrations responsible for this area are not at all familiar with these procedures. in this decision, we must avoid anything that could increase their workload and delay the process, not to mention that the sums involved are not huge at the moment and that the adoption of the decision during this year for the year 2000 will leave little time to prepare the requests for co-financing. the commission proposes to draw inspiration from some of the ideas put forward in the amendments in the context of the definition of the practical modalities for implementing this instrument and the dialogue it will establish with the national services responsible. finally, as regards the amendments concerning cooperation with the applicant countries, i think we must be very clear. the fund aims to contribute to a balance of effort between member states. these already modest resources should not be diluted by secondary objectives. such cooperation with the candidate countries would be duplicated with other programmes, especially the phare programme on the transposition of the acquis in the field of legislation and the upgrading of the competent administrations in the countries of central and eastern europe. in conclusion, mr president, the commission welcomes the support of the european parliament for this initiative. i believe that we are starting today, together, a journey in the name of fidelity to the values of asylum, a journey to demonstrate that we can all rise to the challenge of european solidarity in the field of asylum.
- thank you very much, mr. vitorino. the debate is closed. the vote will take place tomorrow at 12 noon.

- question no 33 by mrs pasqualina napoletano (h-0298/00) subject: measures to protect chocolate as part of the quality policy for agricultural products and foodstuffs, the european union has set up systems for the protection of traditional specialities, which also allow chocolate to be recognised as having this quality. council regulation (eec) no 2088/92 of 14 july 1992 on the certification of the specific character of agricultural products and foodstuffs oj l 208, 24.7.1992, p. 9 provides that the commission is to set up and maintain a register of certification of the specific character of products: on the basis of this register, producers of chocolate made without vegetable fat other than cocoa butter may apply for certification of the specific character (guaranteed traditional speciality) in order to be recognised as a foodstuff produced from traditional raw materials. could the commission say whether member states have already sent it requests from producers wishing to have the chocolate thus produced entered in the register of specific certificates? is the commission prepared to use all the instruments necessary to implement the provisions of the regulation and to include chocolate without added vegetable fat among the foodstuffs labelled with the gst ('traditional speciality guaranteed') label?
commission (de) mr president, madam member, as i have already said, no chocolate manufacturer has so far shown any interest in such protection. we have no requests. however, in order to satisfy your desire for a more detailed presentation, i should like to draw your attention to the fact that the regulation i have mentioned provides in principle for two possibilities of legal protection of descriptions. the first possibility is that a description can only be protected if it is associated with the community designation of origin and the community logo associated with it. in such a case, other products may be found on the market with the same name as the registered product but produced by a different method and therefore not entitled to bear the community name and logo. that is the drawback of this variant. second possibility: a description may be protected as such if it corresponds to a unique and registered production method. in such a case, it is no longer possible to find a product of the same description on the market produced under different conditions. registration of the description 'chocolate' accompanied by a certificate of specificity would therefore only be possible under the first procedure. following the second procedure, the registration would be contrary to the future chocolate directive because chocolate is the subject of a new definition and may contain a certain percentage of vegetable fats other than cocoa butter.

- question no 38 by mr göran färm (h-0287/00): subject: structural measures to deal with late payments the community budget is unbalanced because commitments are followed by corresponding payments only to a very small extent. the actual share of payments in total commitments has been declining for many years and is estimated to be barely 80%. this is partly a consequence of the delays in the implementation of the union's projects. the absurdity of the system is becoming more and more apparent. the member states are committed to financing activities under the aegis of the union, while, due to the delay in their implementation, the projects have long lost their legitimacy but are nevertheless still financed. this is intolerable, especially in view of the negative opinion of the union in a number of member states. can the commission indicate what structural measures it considers necessary to remedy the delay in payments? questions to mr kinnock
commission (de) mr president, the commission is doing everything it can to settle regular payment requests within 60 days. the vast majority of invoices can be paid within this time limit and, fortunately, the number of overruns is decreasing. however, the honourable member's question is clearly not limited to the execution of payments in the strict sense but also concerns the question of the total number of commitments still to be settled arising from previous budgetary years. in practical terms, this is the time between the first commitment and a concrete contract and the time between the commitment and the actual payment of resources. last year the commission presented a working paper to the budgetary authority which contained an in-depth analysis of the trend - broken down by sector and underlying factors - and proposed remedial measures. this analysis is currently being updated by the commission. in terms of volume, the sum of commitments to be converted into payments in subsequent years was about eur 71 billion at the end of 1999. in fact, the evolution of the past burden is influenced by several factors and i think it is important to establish this clearly. the first factor is the ratio of commitment appropriations to payment appropriations established each year in the budget by the budgetary authority. for example, for the year 2000, it was decided to include in the budgetary plan commitments exceeding payment appropriations by some eur 4 billion as a means of payment. the second factor concerns the call for these budgetary resources, both commitment and payment authorizations. finally, a not insignificant role is played by the release of resources for which there is no longer any need to wait for a request for payment, the so-called dormant commitments - a somewhat misleading term - which will clearly no longer be converted into concrete commitments and into concrete payment obligations. however, the commission cannot agree with the honourable member's view that the delay in the implementation of community projects systematically deprives them of all legitimacy, quite the contrary. as soon as the commission reaches the conclusion that there is no longer any need to wait for a substantiated request for payment in respect of a project, for example in the event of suspension or abandonment of the project, it shall request the release of the corresponding commitment. in 1999, this was the case for an amount of nearly one billion euros. i should like to stress that many of the union's programmes are characterised by a time lag between the overall authorizations for commitments and their implementation in concrete projects. this is the case, for example, of multiannual programmes, the most important of which in terms of quantity are the structural funds, which are managed separately: the commission issues authorizations for commitments and these are then implemented in concrete projects at member state level. in order to reduce the time lag between promises, actual implementation and payments, it is important, first, that the budgetary authority decides on a balanced ratio between commitment and payment authorizations and, second, that there is in fact a pressure to accelerate the implementation of the programmes. the commission has discussed this today in the context of the revision of the financial regulation and i can assure you that we are changing the rules in order to tighten the process over time. i hope you will support me in this.
commission - (de) mr president, an analysis has shown that the implementation of the commitments for concrete projects takes about a year and a half. that is very good, but there are also old commitments, dormant commitments, and i can tell you that recently 20 additional posts were added to the 60 posts which were decided last december to be made available to the scr in order to examine which commitments were no longer linked to any commitments and could therefore be wound up. i thank you very much for your suggestion. this is precisely the path the commission will take in the context of the revision of the financial regulation and i am therefore already certain that i have a supporter in parliament.
commission - (de) mr president, it is absolutely essential for the union's reputation to reduce the gap between what i will call concrete promises and contracts and to make payments as soon as invoices are received, i.e. when there are valid requests for payment. it is clear that benchmarking is about not letting 60 days pass and, as i said, an increasing number of payments are being settled within that time. of course, the aim is to eliminate as far as possible any exceptions.

i will come back to that in a moment. i would like to make a few additional remarks which were raised in lisbon and which we are following up. first of all, we have been instructed by the commission to draw up a package of proposals concerning concessions for the region in the area of asymmetric trade. it is worth remembering that total exports from the balkans to the european union represent about 0.6% of our total imports. for agricultural products, the figures are about 0.16%. so we can afford to be a little more generous in this area. we are also trying to speed up the delivery of aid and make it more effective. i announced yesterday that there was agreement in the commission on a rapid reaction mechanism. we will be presenting to parliament in the coming months our new regulation on aid to the western balkans, which i hope will make it faster, more flexible and which, of course, must include sufficient funds for projects supporting gender issues. i know of no successful model of economic or political development whose core does not include sensible programmes to ensure that women can fulfil their full potential and play their part in their communities. a note on education: last winter, despite all the cynical comments, our programme 'energy for democracy' was extraordinarily successful in serbia. unfortunately, there are few occasions when the european union is cheered on the streets - counsel. - (pt) as you know, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european council in helsinki has given the portuguese presidency the mandate to set up the interim defence and security structures within the union as from 1 march this year. these structures were set up on 1 march and all the activities aimed at putting them into practice, and in particular giving shape to the final model, are currently taking place. we think this model will be operational next year. in parallel with these practical aspects, a discussion is currently taking place within the european union with a view to putting into practice the mechanisms for the participation of both european union countries which are not members of nato and nato countries which are not members of the european union, within the general framework of the action of the so-called petersberg tasks provided for by the treaty of amsterdam. the question which arises and which is also raised by the honourable member - whom i thank because i have the responsibility of chairing the preparatory group for the intergovernmental conference - is to what extent this question will or will not be raised in the context of the conference. it will be raised at the conference only if it is necessary to amend the treaty on european union in order to give practical follow-up to the functioning of these structures. at the present stage of the debate within the european union, it is not yet clear that the treaty needs to be amended. as soon as it becomes clear, we will say so. we will report to the european council in santa maria da feira in june, where we will assess the state of progress and decide whether or not these matters should be included in the intergovernmental conference. if this integration is to take place, it can only be during the french presidency.
- (pt) mr president, there is no doubt that there is confusion in your question, unless it is a matter of misinterpretation. today we are not talking about defence policy, we are talking about crisis management, which is currently enshrined in the treaties. there is no question of a european defence policy, there is no question of creating a european army. it is a question of crisis management, humanitarian action, what is commonly known in community parlance as the 'petersberg tasks'. in these missions, all the countries of the european union are providing valuable assistance, including your own country, mr president. we do not want to create a european defence policy, but a common security culture that will enable us to work together on crisis management. i do not think there are any major difficulties in this area. we hope to reconcile all the different cultures of the union.
- (pt) the humanitarian and crisis management actions envisaged by the petersberg tasks, to which the helsinki european council refers, are actions that can be carried out within the framework of the european union, but we intend to ensure that these actions will all be compatible with what exists today in the relationship between certain countries of the european union and the countries of nato. why would you do that ? because the mechanisms and means available for dealing with these crises are not immense, they are, for the most part, precisely those of nato. the means of military and security action which exist today within the framework of the union and nato will be mobilised. it is important to ensure effective collaboration with all nato countries; and when we talk about the nato countries, we're talking about the countries that are not part of the european union, especially the candidate countries like turkey, norway and iceland. it is obvious that in a broader sense and in view of the scale of the operations, we are also talking about the united states and canada. it is therefore a broader form of cooperation which is intended to guarantee a sharing of responsibilities between all those who today share the same objective and the same culture of defence and security.
question no 13 by mr papayannakis, substitute for mr sjöstedt (h-0283/00) subject: violation of the right to freedom of expression recently, the one-man trial court in thessalonica banned the distribution of a book by the writer mimi androulakis on the grounds of "irreverence". since, in the words of article 6 of the amsterdam treaty, 'the union is founded on the principles of liberty, democracy and respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms' and in the dual consideration that greece is a contracting party to the european convention for the protection of human rights, which guarantees the right to freedom of expression and freedom of conscience, on the one hand, and that the basic element of the europe of citizens lies in its fundamental attachment to freedom, pluralism and human rights, on the other hand, could the council comment on the inspiration behind measures of this nature? does the commission intend to take action before the competent greek authorities to bring an end to the prosecution of the author and to lift the ban on the sale of his book?
counsel. - (pt) mr papayannakis asks the council how it interprets the decision of the thessaloniki court of first instance prohibiting the distribution of a book by the writer androlakis, which it considers heretical; the council is not prepared to accept the commission's proposal. i would like to say that under article 6 (1) of the treaty on european union, the treaty of amsterdam, the union respects a set of basic principles through a reference to the european convention on human rights and fundamental freedoms. the philosophy behind this article is to establish a kind of political control over the actions of the member states and to ensure that democratic values and principles are respected. this article aims to ensure the sharing of common values. but article 6 cannot be invoked to interfere in any way with the administration of the internal affairs of the member states, particularly at the level of justice. the union shall not have competence to intervene in the exercise of the judicial power of the member states. the council cannot therefore intervene in the decision-making of the authorities. the measure adopted by the court of first instance of thessaloniki, which is a measure of a judicial body of a member state, relating to a specific case, is subject to appeal, within the framework of the greek judicial system, to the higher instances. once the appeals to the greek courts have been exhausted, there is still the possibility of bringing the case before the human rights court.
- (pt) mr president, the member states undertake to act within the framework laid down by the treaty. that's why they signed the treaty. in the event of a serious and persistent violation of the rights of citizens, there are of course means of intervening with these states under the provisions of these articles. the union has the means to intervene with the states. but let us be realistic: in this case, in a democratic country like greece, this is a case which fulfils all the conditions for being tried and evolving within the greek judicial system until the possibilities of appeal provided by this system are exhausted. otherwise we would obviously be transposing a matter to the community level for which there is a whole range of remedies in a country which fully respects human and civil rights.

- the next item is the joint debate on the following reports: - a5-0059/2000 by mr garcía-margallo y marfil, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy, on the communication from the commission on the implementation of the framework for action in the financial services sector: action plan (com (99) 232 - c5-0114/1999 1999/2117 (cos)) - a5-0053/2000 by mr kuckelkorn, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the commission communication 'towards a single market for supplementary pensions - outcome of the consultation on the green paper on supplementary pensions in the single market (com (99) 134 - c5-0135/1999 - 1999/2131 (cos)) '. before i begin, i would like to say to my colleagues that as this is an evening sitting and we have a lot of work to do, i will make a very careful use of speaking time. i therefore ask members to exercise discipline so that we can finish at a decent hour.
the rapporteur. - (es) mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i would like to thank you for your reply. if i were to mention two complex economic issues here today, i would not hesitate to mention them: the consolidation of financial markets and the approximation of the standards of direct taxation - specifically, taxation on savings - which are currently under discussion. the recent debate on collective investment schemes and the reactions to the report on pension funds which will be discussed later demonstrate the complexity and importance of these issues. the two topics, financial services market liberalisation and taxation, are addressed in the action plan which is the subject of my report. it is therefore right to thank all the groups for their cooperation and to reassure the commission that it can count on the active collaboration of the european parliament in the development of this plan, without abandoning its powers but exercising them in a responsible manner. the complexity of the action plan also meets the ambition of the report presented by the commission, which includes 43 measures, covering all sectors of the field (stock exchanges, banks, investment funds, insurance, etc.) and which is part of what has been called the new economy, which - after the lisbon summit - is one of the remedies to put an end to unemployment in europe. what are these measures? what is their purpose? in my view, the answer is to liberalise the financial sectors and to update the standards of supervision and control so that the european financial market is at least as competitive as the us market. in the explanatory memorandum, i shall devote a long comment to the comparison between the two types of market. to achieve these two objectives, the commission proposes a formula which is certainly questionable and risky: the acceleration of the legislative process, which in turn would be achieved by three actions. firstly, the reduction of the standards which need to be included in a regulation or directive, namely those which require the involvement of this parliament. secondly, the limitation of these standards to the definition of the general criteria and basic principles to be developed in this field, thus leaving the commission the possibility of developing them. and thirdly, the granting of broad powers of interpretation to the commission. i am convinced that the process must be speeded up, commissioner, but this parliament is not prepared to give up the powers it has taken so long to acquire. so one of the first tasks we will have to carry out together will be to find a model which will satisfy both objectives. as regards liberalisation, the first of the tasks proposed by the commission, the commission is guided by the principle that consolidation of the single market for financial services requires the removal of the obstacles which make it difficult to operate. we couldn't agree more. the corollary of this is that these barriers must be removed if the market is to function. we also agree, but we know that this path is fraught with obstacles, which are due to the need to reconcile the objective of liberalisation with the objective of investor protection. first, the obstacles are not identified. it is not enough, commissioner, to be able to deduce them from reading the measures proposed by the commission. i would personally have liked to have a list of the national measures which, in accordance with the financial services directive, make it difficult for the market to function in each country. secondly, the solution proposed by the commission continues to present problems. it is aberrant that a financial undertaking should act in compliance with and with knowledge of fifteen legal orders, but it is equally aberrant if an investor - at least a lay investor - is obliged to purchase services from companies whose legal regulations he is unaware of, whose solvency he is unaware of, and, in the event of a dispute, to be sued in a foreign country, a foreign court and a foreign procedure. liberalisation must therefore develop in parallel with the increase in control measures and the prosecution service. as regards control measures, we are faced with a new problem: the need to adapt to a different world - characterised by globalisation, international competition and the free movement of capital - competition and the jurisdictions of authorities which remain national and which apply for the most part different models. finally, mr president, i am personally convinced that if we do not want liberalisation to lead to distortions of competition and to flight to milder climates inside and outside the union, the proper functioning of the financial services market will not be possible without a certain approximation of the standards governing savings. these are the concerns raised by my report; i would like to say that i am very pleased that the commission has taken the initiative to present this report, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. - (es) mr president, i will speak - as you said on behalf of the committee on legal affairs and the internal market - about the commission's communication on the action plan for the implementation of the financial services framework. as the lead rapporteur, mr garcía-margallo, has pointed out, this aspect includes two issues, namely, firstly, taxation - without tax harmonization, it would be very difficult for community financial services to exist - and secondly, the legal framework. as for the legal framework, i think there is a paradox in this sector. the more liberalized an economy is, the more strictly regulated financial services are needed. the us economy, which is probably one of the most liberalised economies to date, is the one that sets the most detailed regulations on financial services. the commission, in its proposal, on page 18 of the spanish text, after having recognised the competence of the parliament through co-decision, in accordance with article 251 of the treaty, tells us that we should strive for more flexible procedures through comitology. comitology often involves taking back with one hand what is given with the other. in this respect, i fully agree with the rapporteur's conclusions. i think that very specific legislative development is needed and i am sure that the commission can count on parliament's support for this legislative development. as the rapporteur said a moment ago, we cannot hope to gain the confidence of investors, consumers and, ultimately, the financial services sector, if there is no clear legal framework. the only way to achieve this is to replace the rigid regulations currently in force with precise community rules to ensure safety in this very sensitive sector of the economy.
- (es) mr president, on behalf of the green group, i would like to express my opinion on the single market for supplementary pension schemes. firstly, i would like to say that we agree with the intergenerational solidarity scheme of the national basic schemes, to which are added the complementary schemes by capitalisation. on the other hand, i would also like to say that i agree with what mr kuckelkorn says about the correlation between social security systems and the coverage of biometric risks. we are not talking about investment schemes but pension plans. on the other hand, we also agree with worker participation and the urgent harmonisation of tax regulations. however, the concept of pension funds needs to be clarified and include complementary prevention systems covering biometric risks. it should also be made clear that the single system concerns all types of workers in the european union; there are not only wage-earners in the european union, there are also many cooperative workers, fortunately. we must rely on collective systems, not just within companies - this principle is already in the report - but also on sectoral systems, taking into account in particular smes, which were mentioned by mrs plooij-van gorsel. account should be taken of the wide differences in the development of complementary systems within the union. we therefore understand and support the regulatory and control systems to defend the rights of beneficiaries, but where the systems are still not fully developed, emphasis will have to be placed on aspects such as information or the implementation of new plans. finally, i would like to stress our support for the creation of a european pension fund with the participation of the various sectors of economic activity and providers.

developments in the action plan; every six months we send a progress report to the ecofin council and i think these reports are useful for exchanging ideas with parliament. mr president, most of the rights of future pensioners. no, that's not the case. however, investment and management rules may serve interests other than the protection of the beneficiaries. unnecessary provisions that reduce investment results are against the interests of the beneficiaries and must therefore be abolished. the second point concerns the coordination of the tax systems of the member states and is a labour migration. the commission is currently preparing a draft general framework to facilitate the payment of benefits by occupational pension funds established in another member state. this general framework is of course also the subject of a request made in this house, by mr medina ortega for example, while the commission is not the only one to have made a request for it. mrs peijs also the amendments, i would like to emphasize the point of scope. the scope of the future proposal - as the directive is not yet ready - for a directive on the regulation of the activities of occupational pension funds. the question is therefore - and many members in this house have raised this issue, in particular mrs kauppi - whether the proposal we are about to table should cover all forms of pension savings, or whether it should be more simply limited to those forms of pension savings which protect savers against biometric risks? my answer to that question is this, and i hope it is clear: we need european prudential standards applicable to all forms of occupational pension savings. these standards will differ in some respects according to the actual risks covered by these institutions. but there is no technical reason why these different forms of saving should not be covered by a single directive. it would be unfair, in my view, and would artificially restrict the european union, if the commission limited the proposed directive to pension schemes covering only biometric risks to the exclusion of other pension savings which are indeed forms of pension savings since they cannot be paid to the beneficiary before he has reached retirement age. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: i don't think that's fair. i don't think that's fair. i don't think that is fair. i think that the european union would not be doing itself a favour by limiting the scope of the directive to biometric risks, and quite frankly, i do not see why other forms of pension savings should not be included as i have just said. member states will therefore have a wide margin of manoeuvre to promote, for example through tax measures, certain pension schemes which they would like to stimulate more particularly. they also have the option of requiring that products offered on their national market meet certain social criteria even if they are offered by providers established in another member state. employees and employers in the same company or sector are free to choose according to the advantages and disadvantages of the products they can obtain in their market. the freedom of choice of the member states therefore remains to a large extent, leaving them the possibility to organise pension schemes in their territory as they see fit. that freedom remains. what the commission is seeking is a framework that liberalises the constitution and scope of pension funds for the benefit of the people who contribute to them. we must therefore create within the european union this legal framework which will enable businesses and future pensioners to choose in a transparent market the products offered by bodies subject to adequate control. proper control is essential, as is the liberalisation of the scope of the funds concerned. the role of the commission is not to specify in detail what a pension savings product should be, this is a competence of the member states under the principle of subsidiarity and the commission does not intend to undertake anything that goes against this principle.

- the next item is the report (a5-0098/2000) by mrs palacio vallelersundi, on behalf of the committee on legal affairs and the internal market, on the communication from the commission to the european parliament and the council: 'a strategy for the european internal market' (com (99) 464 - c5-0212/1999 - 1999/2167 (cos)).
the rapporteur. - (es) mr president, commissioner, the report i have the honour of presenting is the result of an extraordinary collaboration - which i welcome - between individuals and committees. let me make two points: the legal affairs committee has not accepted all the suggestions from the committees responsible for opinions. we were in full agreement with many of them and found them very interesting, but we felt that they had no place in this resolution and that their inclusion would have made the message less clear. that was my criterion when i recommended that the amendments tabled in the house be voted in favour. i would also like to stress that - and the opinion of the committee on fisheries is a good example of this - we did not include them in the resolution not because we rejected their content, but because we felt that the message of the internal market strategy should be clear. what was the message? this message is rooted in the position adopted by the legal affairs committee in our resolution of 4 november 1999. if i may, mr president, i would like to focus on three ideas. the first concern of the legal affairs committee - and i hope that the house will ratify it tomorrow - is the situation of the internal market. what is the internal market in the construction of europe? today we hear the sirens of globalisation singing and at the same time the idea that we are international is emerging. the internal market has become too small in this new globalised economy. that's absolutely not true. this is clearly underlined in the single market strategy. the internal market is europe's platform in the world. the internal market contains the core principles of a globalised economy with competitive advantages for europe. that is the first message from the legal affairs committee. the principles of the internal market must be emphasized: the principle of proportionality, the principle of mutual recognition, the principle of control at the source. these must be the main pillars on which this internal market strategy must be based. of course, this won't make the headlines, but it's important. how important is the application and monitoring of community legislation; enforcement for which the member states must cooperate. we must oppose the procedures which are too often used, such as gold plating. we must strengthen our procedure in the event of an infringement, we must consolidate it, make it more transparent, more accessible. we ask that decisions to close infringement cases be reasoned and that parliament be informed of them. we ask that infringement cases be dealt with more quickly and better presented to the citizen. the second message of this resolution is that we must transform the more or less disorderly legislation we have today, which the citizen perceives as a burden, into a genuine legal order, into a coherent and clear regulatory framework, without disguises or contradictions. these small contradictions are perceived by the citizen and by the industry as burdens, as a lack of clarity in the message about the path being taken. finally, the third message is a change in the business culture in europe. business owners need to be more able to take risks. to do this we will have to change some laws, such as the european laws on insolvency in general, on cessation of payments and bankruptcies. we must insist on the creation of a genuine venture capital market. we must ensure that young europeans are convinced, as are young americans, that the best outcome of education is not to join a large company, to have a long career there, but to create new companies. to do this, the e-commerce environment, the environment of new technologies must provide a good platform. in conclusion, mr president, and in summary, i hope that tomorrow, when we vote on this resolution, parliament will put forward a clear idea. we support the commission in this initiative and in any case we want to be involved in the whole cycle, on a permanent basis, by collaborating, giving ideas and exercising control.
